title: Real analysis II: metric spaces, uniform convergence and several variables
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Extend analysis beyond the real line: metric spaces, open and closed sets, completeness and compactness, continuity and connectedness, sequences and series of functions and uniform convergence, power series, the Weierstrass approximation and Arzelà–Ascoli theorems, the contraction mapping principle, derivatives of maps between Euclidean spaces, the inverse and implicit function theorems, and multiple integrals.
primary_reading: Basic Analysis I and II by Jiří Lebl (free online)

weeks.1: Metric spaces, open and closed sets
weeks.4: Continuity, uniform continuity and connectedness in metric spaces
weeks.5: Sequences and series of functions: pointwise and uniform convergence
weeks.6: Interchanging limits with derivatives and integrals
weeks.7: Power series and the Weierstrass approximation theorem
weeks.10: Derivatives of maps between Euclidean spaces
weeks.11: The inverse and implicit function theorems
weeks.12: Multiple integrals and change of variables

blocks.deliverable: Prove that a supplied metric space is complete or exhibit a Cauchy sequence that does not converge.
Prove that a continuous function on a compact metric space attains its extreme values and is uniformly continuous.
Decide which supplied sequences converge uniformly and justify each interchange of limits.
Week 7 midterm; prove that a power series converges uniformly on compact subintervals of its interval of convergence.
Use the contraction mapping principle to solve an equation and bound the error of the iteration.
Apply the implicit function theorem to a supplied system of equations.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Analysis portfolio: prove the Arzelà–Ascoli theorem and the inverse function theorem in full with every step justified, implement Picard iteration in plain Python for two initial value problems and compare its convergence with the contraction estimate, and write a short exposition of three counterexamples that show why uniform convergence matters.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
